result.summary: Implemented the CLM-017 claims-and-documentation CI gate: a pure typed manifest/orchestration module (src/lib/ci/claims-docs-gate.ts) mapping 11 checks to the 7 required Done-when categories, reusing existing npm validators (public-claims, numeric-claims, content-templates, doc-sources, doc-references, api-docs, unit tests, pulse-runtime, metadata, terminology, policy-surface) without duplicating their logic. Added scripts/validate-claims-docs.ts (npm run validate:claims-docs) which first proves seeded stale-copy fixtures fail closed per category in-process, then runs every child validator, reports each result, and exits nonzero on any failure. Added a pure test suite proving manifest validation (duplicate/missing/unknown category rejection), evaluateGate semantics, and that every category's seeded fixture independently fails the gate. Added .github/workflows/claims-docs.yml (push/PR, Node 22, npm ci, npm run validate:claims-docs — no DB/secrets needed since content-templates soft-fails without DATABASE_URL). Simplified npm run build to: sync-freshness && replication-surface && editorial-illustrations && validate:claims-docs && next build. Documented the command in README.template.md (regenerated README.md) and AGENTS.md's Committing section.
result.verification: Focused gate tests (9 new tests) pass within the 321-test full suite; npm run validate:claims-docs passes end-to-end locally without touching any owned scope outside the brief; npm run typecheck and targeted eslint on new files are clean; validate:doc-references (README/route/file-pointer sync) passes; git diff --check clean; content-templates validator soft-fails gracefully without DATABASE_URL, confirming the gate works in a DB-less CI runner. Not committed, per instructions.
